title: Quantization + Batching Node Allocation Snapshot (throughput vs quality)
summary: Working capacity snapshot comparing node allocation strategies when using mixed quantization profiles and batching windows. Focus: region-aware placement, utilization headroom, and tolerable quality delta for customer-facing latencies.
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sheet to capture a draft node allocation plan that trades quantization (int8 / int4 / awq) and batching aggressiveness against measured quality delta and latency SLOs. Goal: produce an allocation that meets 95th pctl latency <= 220ms for interactive routes while maximizing throughput and keeping perceptual quality delta < 0.8% (internal eval metric).

Key constraints / inputs (assumptions):
- Fleet available (global): 120 active GPU nodes (mix: 40 H100-80GB, 50 A100-80GB, 30 L4).
- Average hourly demand (global) baseline: 1.6M tokens / hour (current prod mix).
- Expected growth for next quarter: +28% traffic.
- Workload mix: 60% chat (latency-sensitive), 30% generation (throughput-oriented), 10% embeddings/rerank (batch-friendly).
- Acceptable eval delta thresholds (from product): quality_delta_chat <= 0.8% , generation_bleu_drop <= 1.2%.

Quantization profiles tested (measured on representative model x-2b):
- FP16 baseline: latency per token (H100): 2.8ms; throughput (tokens/sec per node): 360
- int8 (layerwise symmetric): latency 2.1ms; throughput 480; measured quality delta 0.35%
- awq4 (aggressive 4-bit): latency 1.7ms; throughput 600; measured quality delta 1.6%
- hybrid int8+awq (KV-cache hot layers int8, attention awq): latency 1.9ms; throughput 540; quality delta 0.9%

Batching window experiments (simulated):
- 0ms (no explicit batching): baseline latency numbers above, utilization low for chat routes (~28% avg GPU utilization).
- 20ms max wait: increases throughput +18% relative to no-batching for chat-heavy nodes, p95 latency +12ms.
- 50ms max wait: increases throughput +42% but p95 latency +48ms (exceeds interactive SLO).

Scenario A: Latency-first (chat SLO priority)
- Node mix allocated to chat regions (NA / EU): dedicate 60 H100 nodes to chat routes, configured hybrid int8+awq, batching window 20ms.
- Remaining nodes: 40 A100 / 20 L4 for generation/embeddings with int8, 50ms batching allowed for generation queues.
- Expected global utilization: chat nodes 62% avg, generation nodes 78% avg.
- Expected p95 latency (chat): ~205ms (within 220ms).
- Quality: chat quality delta ~0.95% (slightly above product goal of 0.8) -> requires review: possibility: flip chat nodes to int8-only to reduce delta (cost: -12% throughput).

Scenario B: Throughput-first (cost-sensitive)
- Aggressive quantization across fleet: 70% nodes set to awq4, batching windows 50ms where safe.
- Node mix: keep H100s prioritized for highest concurrency shards; A100/L4 handle burst.
- Expected throughput uplift: +33% tokens/hr; utilization bumped to 85% overall.
- p95 latency (chat): ~265ms (violates SLO).
- Quality: generation eval drop within tolerable 1.2% but chat quality delta 1.6% (too high).

Scenario C: Region-aware hybrid (recommended starting point)
- NA/EU: keep 55 H100s hybrid-int8 (KV-cache int8, rest awq) with 20ms batching for chat. Latency target prioritized.
- APAC: deploy 15 L4 for embeddings-heavy workloads and opportunistic generation at int8, batching 50ms.
- Global soft-pool (20 nodes): awq4, placed in low-cost region for bulk batch rerank/embeddings.
- Expected p95 latency (chat): ~215ms. Quality deltas: chat 0.78% (meets target), generation 1.0%. Utilization: NA/EU chat nodes 68%, APAC L4 72%, soft-pool 88%.

Risk checklist / open questions:
- Eval coverage: current quality deltas come from a 1k-prompt synthetic eval set (mostly English). Need multilingual samples for APAC customers.
- Cold start KV-cache behavior: hybrid profiles rely on warm KV caches; initial latency spike not fully captured in lab tests. Add mitigation: cache warmers for canary rollouts.
- Network egress costs when routing to soft-pool in cheaper region — need finance estimate for cross-region traffic.
- Autoscaling granularity: current autoscaler scales nodes in 1-node increments. For hybrid quant profiles, scaling steps can cause noticeable SLO jitter; consider smaller increment or pre-warmed spare nodes.

Quick numbers table (snapshot):
- Fleet: 120 nodes total
- Alloc (Scenario C): H100: 55 (chat), A100: 30 (gen/mix), L4: 15 (APAC embed), soft-pool: 20 (awq batch)
- Estimated tokens/hr capacity (Scenario C): 2.1M tokens/hr (peak)
- Estimated monthly hours used (billable node-hrs): 120 nodes * 24 * 30 * utilization-average("Estimated avg util"=0.73) -> ~63,072 node-hrs/month (rounded)

Operational runbook notes (short):
- Canary rollout plan: 1) enable hybrid-int8 on 3 H100 nodes in NA, 2) route 1% traffic, monitor p95 latency and quality metrics for 24h, 3) expand to 20% if no regressions.
- Rollback triggers: chat p95 > 230ms sustained for 15m OR quality_regression_metric > 1.2% on canary prompts.
- Monitoring hooks: add per-node quant_profile tag to telemetry so we can correlate latency & token-cost.

Decisions to make this week:
- Approve Scenario C as baseline for Q3 ramp and sign-off on cache warming strategy (owner: Marcus Patel).
- Finance to model cross-region egress impact for the 20-node soft-pool (owner: Sofia Morales).
- Research to expand eval set to multilingual + long-context prompts before APAC rollout (owner: Lin Zhao).

Draft TODOs (engineering):
- [ ] Add quant_profile label to node metadata and surface in Console (INFRA-732)
- [ ] Implement cache warmer job + test on canary nodes
- [ ] Add batching window as runtime-configurable per-route (prod flag)
- [ ] Run a 72h stress test with 28% traffic growth synthetic workload and capture p95/p99/quality timeline

Notes to self (informal):
- We are currently leaning hybrid-int8 in chat regions because it consistently keeps p95 near target while reducing quality regressions vs full awq. If product tolerances loosen, we can swing awq more broadly to save cost.
- Need to keep close to Console team for per-route batching flags so we can A/B different batching windows without redeploying runtime.

Appendix: quick eval snippets (high level):
- eval set: 1k prompts, mix: 70% chat-style, 20% long-form generation, 10% rerank
- quality metric: composite score (semantic-similarity + factual-consistency heuristic), baseline normalized to 100. Deltas listed above are percent drops relative to baseline.

References / links in doc body:
- Linear: INFRA-732 node allocation (above)
- Runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime PR#981 (perf kernels for awq)
- Slack convo: #infra-quant-batching (see thread pinned messages)

End of snapshot. This is intentionally a working sheet — expect numbers to change after multilingual evals and finance egress calc.
